children: The U.S. Department of the Treasury on Thursday sold $25B in 30-year bonds
on Thursday at a high yield of 5.441%, trailing pre-auction expectations as demand softened.
The clearing rate landed 0.4 basis points above the 5.437% when-issued yield, producing a tail that indicated investors required a slight concession to absorb the supply.

Although the high yield marked a decline from the 5.618% yield at the previous 30-year sale, overall bidding appetite cooled, with the bid-to-cover ratio falling to 2.36 from 2.54 in the prior auction.
Furthermore, indirect bidders took 68.1% of the offering, down from 72.3% previously, while direct bidders accounted for 20.5%, edging lower from 20.9% at the last sale.

At the time of writing, the 30-year tenor was yielding 5.44%, up nearly eight basis points on the day and around 17 bps over the last five trading sessions. The U.S. bond market was closed on Wednesday in observance of Veterans Day.
